A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PE3R, with matching authors, core pipeline, benchmarks, and figures. All pages are readable, including v2's supplement; relocated proofs and renamed components can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, depth-estimation, runtime, and component-ablation results in Tables 1–6 and qualitative experiments in Figures 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a VGGT-backed evaluation, aggregation experiments, and supplementary sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline remains. However, v1 replaces anomalous pixels' RGB values with their semantic-region mean, whereas v2 specifies blending that mean with the original value and selects alpha=0.1 (Section 3.4 and Supplement Section 7.3). This changes the reported refinement procedure; expanded tracking details alone do not establish another algorithm change.

E1.justification: The same eight datasets, open-vocabulary segmentation and depth-estimation tasks, and indoor/outdoor coverage remain. RobustMVD explicitly names the existing five-dataset depth benchmark. Additional backbones and parameter studies do not establish new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds OpenNeRF and LSM, and Table 3 adds LSM embeddings. Table 4 adds Fast3R and VGGT while removing MVSNet variants, Vis-MVSNet, MVS2D, DeMoN, DeepV2D, and Robust MVD comparison rows. This substantially revises the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds a VGGT-backbone configuration and controlled sweeps over anomaly thresholds, window sizes, smoothing strengths, and refinement iterations. Table 4 removes the legacy pose/depth-range/alignment-specific comparison groups. Core metrics remain unchanged; newly documented four-frame processing and projection procedures do not establish that existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component-removal studies, v2 Table 6 compares uniform, area-weighted, and confidence-weighted aggregation strategies. Supplement Tables 8–11 test anomaly thresholds, neighborhood size, smoothing strength, and repeated refinement, substantially expanding evidence about design choices and sensitivity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new confidence-weighted aggregation methods and refinement iterations concern algorithm settings, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Most retained benchmark scores are identical, but v2 adds substantial baseline and ablation results and removes legacy depth rows. New VGGT-backed PE3R reports average rel/tau of 3.7/75.2, while the retained DUSt3R-backed result remains 4.5/68.0; these are different configurations. The no-semantic-reconstruction ablation changes from 5.3/60.2 in v1 Table 6 to 4.9/64.4 in v2 Table 7.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 5 introduces a parameterized mathematical definition of RGB refinement, replacing v1's full mean replacement. The two interpolation propositions and their proofs are otherwise retained and moved to Supplement Section 6; renaming Semantic Vectorization to Semantic Guidance does not change the proposition or reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims of efficient, zero-shot semantic reconstruction without scene-specific training remain. The abstract changes the quantitative speed claim from a minimum nine-fold speedup to up to nine-fold faster inference, narrowing its stated scope despite unchanged runtime results.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses scene-dependent benefits, attributing weaker ScanNet/DTU performance to repetitive textures, limited viewpoints, and semantic ambiguity. It also interprets the added sensitivity studies through noise suppression, detail preservation, and diminishing refinement returns. These provide specific qualifications absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: SAM/SAM2 initialization and re-detection rules, overlap thresholds, four-frame ScanNet++ processing, shared geometry for embedding comparisons, projection-based evaluation, quasi-optimal source-view selection, A100/i7 hardware, and refinement defaults. Much of this is newly disclosed information rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments. The code link is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for MASt3R-SfM, Spann3R, VGGSfM, Fast3R, VGGT, OpenNeRF, and WildSeg3D, while removing references associated with several discarded depth baselines. The central positioning around semantic guidance and efficient reconstruction remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 creates a dedicated framework subsection, changes component terminology, moves proofs into supplementary material, removes the Impact Statement, and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and caption formatting, relocates Figure 1, substantially restructures Table 4, and adds aggregation and supplementary sensitivity tables. The reconstruction ablation gains a runtime-difference column. The six existing figures retain their visual evidence, with resizing and revised captions.

improvement.justification: The added aggregation controls, sensitivity studies, and explicit evaluation details strengthen design justification and reproducibility relative to v1. These gains outweigh the loss of older depth comparisons, but the improvement is limited: core results largely remain unchanged, and the interpolation proof still incorrectly assumes a+b=1 (v1 Equation 11; v2 Equation 16).
